title: Multiply by eleven: add each digit to its neighbour
explanation:
Eleven is ten plus one, so $n\times11=n\times10+n$: the number shifted one place left, plus the number itself. Splitting a product like this is the distributive property at work [1]. Write the two copies one above the other, offset by one place, and the column sums are each digit plus its right-hand neighbour.

That is the Trachtenberg rule: add the digit to its neighbour, where the neighbour is the digit on the right [2]. For a two-digit number $ab$, the answer is $a$, then $a+b$, then $b$. If $a+b$ is 10 or more, write its last digit and carry the 1 into the left digit.

The same rule works for longer numbers. Imagine a zero at each end, work from right to left, and add each digit to its right-hand neighbour, carrying as needed.
keyIdeas: Each digit of the answer is a digit plus its right-hand neighbour.
Work right to left and carry when a pair sums to 10 or more.

steps: Outer digits stay: the answer starts with 5 and ends with 7.
Add the carry to the left digit: $5+1=6$.

pitfalls: Writing the two-digit pair sum in the middle without carrying (e.g. 5|12|7).
Adding the carry to the wrong digit; it goes to the next digit on the left.
Forgetting the outer digits for numbers with three or more digits.

citations.quote: If you think about doing the math in this way, you are using the Distributive Property.
citations.locator: 7.3 Distributive Property: Simplify Expressions Using the Distributive Property

citations.quote: Rule: Add the digit to its neighbor. (By "neighbor" we mean the digit on the right.)
